result.summary: In the fifth year of Aristodemus's reign, the Lacedaemonians and Messenians meet again, each with allies. Aristodemus uses picked heavy troops and hidden light-armed troops near Ithome to wear out the Spartans, who break and flee.

scenes.title: Allies gather for battle
scenes.summary: Both exhausted nations prepare to fight again. Corinth aids Sparta; Arcadians, Argives and Sicyonians aid Messenia. The Spartans take up an unusually deep formation.
scenes.stakes: Both sides risk defeat after a long, costly war.

scenes.title: Aristodemus arranges his army
scenes.summary: Aristodemus arms strong men with the best weapons, places them among allies, and puts Ithome behind his line. Cleonnis commands there, while light-armed troops lie hidden.
scenes.stakes: Messenia could be outflanked and overwhelmed by the larger Spartan force.

scenes.title: The Spartans are routed
scenes.summary: The Messenian heavy troops hold, and the light troops harass the Spartans, who pursue and break. The Spartans suffer heavy losses, and the Corinthians face a dangerous way home.
scenes.stakes: The Spartans risk destruction; the Corinthians risk attack on the road home.

notable_quotes.reason: Pausanias's brief remark on human psychology explains why the Spartans fell into the trap.

analysis.text: The battle shows cunning and discipline beating numbers. Ambush and light troops let the weaker Messenians outmatch the Spartan phalanx.
The passage describes the First Messenian War, in which Sparta conquered Messenia. Pausanias drew on earlier sources, and the account reflects Messenian tradition.

language_notes.text: "Open proclamation of war" means formal public declaration of war, following Greek custom, rather than a surprise attack.
"Provincials" translates the perioikoi, free but politically subject inhabitants of Laconian towns around Sparta.
"Helots" were the state-owned serf population of Laconia and Messenia, forced to work the land for Spartans.
"Taken in flank" means attacked on the side, where a battle line is weakest; extending the line prevented being outflanked.
"A second danger and so hopeless a one in the same place" means being attacked by light troops while already pressed by heavy infantry.
"Feint" means a pretended retreat meant to draw the enemy out of formation.

context_notes.text: Ithome is the mountain fortress of the Messenians, a natural stronghold that protected their rear from encirclement.
Skins of wolves and bears show the poorer, mountain-bred Arcadian fighters, who lacked metal armour.
Corinth lay north of Argos and Sicyon, which were allied with Messenia, so the Corinthians' route home crossed enemy territory.

literary_notes.text: Quality of picked men is set against the Spartans' 'armed mob', reversing the expected advantage of numbers.
The narrator steps in with a general remark on human psychology to explain why the Spartans lost discipline.
Pausanias openly admits uncertainty about the casualty figures, showing his careful, source-conscious historian's stance.
